title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain: fixed-step walks with a routed six-class key table (no twist index, proved collision law) (v4: direct-bucket chained table, exact multinomial variance, 128-bit counters, 128x unrolled passes, 126.17719)

claims.statement: For every challenge T=[x]P0 in BLS12-381 G1 (T=infinity returns 0), the algorithm in proof.md outputs x with probability at least 0.39 over its own coins, and on every run its total work is at most 2^126.17719 batched-affine-G1-addition equivalents (C=2,000 scalar AArch64 instructions; computed total < 2^126.177180). Algorithm: M=2^63 walks with fresh uniform c_w, b_w and nonzero D_w; walk w visits Q_{w,j}=[c_w+j*D_w]P0+[b_w]T for j=0..L, L=2^63.128335 (n=M(L+1)=2^126.128335 points), each new point one batched incomplete affine addition Q+S_w with the walk's fixed step S_w=[D_w]P0 (one Fermat inversion per batch of 2^24 walks). Each point's six-class key K (y if y even, else p-y; a complete invariant of the class under negation and phi(x,y)=(beta*x,y)=[lambda]) is routed in two hops by AArch64 stores into mapped receive windows (digit1 = bits 1..36 of K, digit2 = bits 0..34 of limb 1) to one of 2^71 final nodes, whose direct-bucket tables (2^57 eight-byte heads each, global load 0.2733, zeroed once, home bucket by extr/umulh) hold 40-byte (next,K1,K2,walk id,j) entries in per-node arenas and scan every bucket chain comparing limbs 1-2 of K; equal keys are candidates, verified by recomputing both points from a walk directory, finding the unit u, and solving x=(u(c_w'+j'D_w')-c_w-jD_w)/(b_w-u*b_w') with [x]P0=T checked. The three table passes are each unrolled 128x, so loop control costs 2/128 per point (the accepted P-256 convention). Cost: per point 1 + 65.080882/2000 units (18 operand-traffic instructions of the reference addition, 12 explicitly charged pass-bookkeeping instructions of the batched addition (prefix-product stores/reloads, loop control), generator 16 + 2/128 for key, digit and remote append, intermediate 8 + 2/128, final main path 11 + 2/128, <0.0141 batch-inversion share, <0.02 round bookkeeping), table zeroing <2^116.10, chain comparisons charged 11 instructions each and allotted at 1.10 times E[X]=n(n-1)/(2*2^128)=2^123.257 by one global 128-bit counter (high-word cap 2^59.394, checked before every comparison), exact integer multinomial Var[X]=2^123.257 and Chebyshev overrun <2^-116.2, candidates capped at 2^90 verifications = 2^104 units by a second global 128-bit counter (mean false candidates 2^87.26; overrun <2^-400), set-up 2^77, routing tables 2^76, capped zero-denominator recovery 2^58, padded window tails 2^113, one round of overshoot <2^85.2; every random action is counted and checked against the global allotment immediately before it runs, walk set-up samples are capped at 128 attempts (failure <2^-371) and zero-denominator recoveries at 4 per generator (failure <2^-120), so the every-run bound uses no round-end aggregation. The collision law is proved (proof.md section 4): the collision events A_w+j*D_w=u(A_w'+j'*D_w') (A_w=c_w+b_w*x uniform) are linear forms in uniform variables, so every intersection has probability r^-rank, all pairs have rank 2 (S2 exact), dependent triples and four-sets contribute < 2^-60 (support/degree argument, integer collinearity, and the norm argument in Z[omega] above r), and Bonferroni gives P >= f4(mu) - 2^-60 with mu=6*C(M,2)*(L+1)^2/r=0.494672 and f4(mu)=mu-mu^2/2+mu^3/6-mu^4/24=0.3900010; failure terms (degenerate b, exceptional additions and zero-denominator batches, conditioning on D!=0, arena/window overflow, global inspection overrun <2^-116.2, candidate overrun <2^-400, sampler caps <2^-371, recovery cap) total < 2^-59, so success >= 0.39 for every x; the abort and overflow bounds use H'. Heuristic H' (routing and bucket bits of K uniform) is used only for the cost-side expectations and concentration (chain comparisons with exact finite multinomial moments, window counts, false candidates, arena occupancy), never for the collision law. Peak memory < 2^132.3 bytes (2^131 B heads + 1.05 n * 40 B arenas; every node < 2^63 bytes with 64-bit addresses); preprocessing (set-up, routing tables, zeroing) < 2^116.2 units, included; no advice.

experiments.purpose: Part A (production BLS12-381 G1): GLV pair and phi(P0)=[lambda]P0, unit map on all six class members, key constant/even/complete, limb-level emulation of the generator key rows (subs/sbcs/tst/csel) against K mod 2^192 and digit1 on random and borrow-chain boundary y, final home index range, AArch64 immediate encodability, chained-insert link consistency, and a planted end-to-end run (real batched affine additions on three walks, planted class collision at a random unit, emulated routing digits and direct-bucket chained table, candidate, recomputation, unit search, solving formula, [x]P0=T). Part B: the whole attack on a toy curve y^2=x^3+4 over F_q with a prime-order subgroup and the same six units (success rate vs 1-exp(-mu) and f4(mu)), and the exact scalar model at small r. Part C: the cost ledger and success bound in exact fractions with checks (including the exact integer multinomial Var[X] and Chebyshev tail <2^-100, the 128-bit inspection and candidate counter listings, the 2^90-verification/2^104-unit candidate cap, the corrected sampler-cap probability, the 128x unroll accounting, and the 1.05 per-node arena margin) (listing lengths counted from the listing text equal the ledger, L from f4, W below the claim, dependency-correction exponents). Toy runs are implementation evidence only; the bound is proved in proof.md.
